content.title: Constricted Route | Continuous Compression Opens into Release
content.summary: Keep high-speed vehicles and cameras bound to the same narrow route, and continuously use walls, arches, drops, and tunnels to compress the available space; in the end, they only pass through the narrowest exit once, and are suddenly released into an unobstructed large-scale environment.

quick_start.input_format: The same vehicle and route axis + at least three gradually narrowing obstacles + the only narrowest threshold + open space release
quick_start.recommended_input: In the original underwater coral maintenance trench, an amber surveying submersible entered at high speed along the basalt trough, and the vehicle was locked before the first narrow section; falling seaweed depressed the space above, two oxidation valve rings rotated across the route, and the submersible continuously passed through the center; the submersible crossed only one exit and entered the top of a huge bioluminescent water basin with no near obstacles. The camera stopped to prove the open scale.
required_anchors: Establish one fast carrier, forward route and coupled camera before the first hard constriction.
Reduce usable clearance progressively with side, overhead and route obstacles.
Use one final tunnel or aperture as the narrowest visible compression.
Cross once into an obstacle-free large environment and let the camera widen or slow.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Keep high-speed vehicles and cameras bound to the same narrow route, and continuously use walls, arches, drops, and tunnels to compress the available space; in the end, they only pass through the narrowest exit once, and are suddenly released into an unobstructed large-scale environment.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Lock a fast carrier and its camera to one continuous constrained route. Escalate by reducing clearance from different sides while preserving forward direction and recurring route geometry. Make one final tunnel or aperture the tightest compression, then cross it exactly once into a materially wider environment where near obstacles disappear and the camera finally slows enough to prove the release.

invariants.rule: Establish one fast carrier, forward route and coupled camera before the first hard constriction.
invariants.ablation_failure: A late carrier reveal makes clearance impossible to judge.

invariants.rule: Reduce usable clearance progressively with side, overhead and route obstacles.
invariants.purpose: Builds pressure through geometry rather than random cuts.

invariants.rule: Keep carrier and camera on the same continuous direction through each opening.
invariants.ablation_failure: Axis resets turn the sequence into disconnected action shots.

invariants.rule: Use one final tunnel or aperture as the narrowest visible compression.
invariants.ablation_failure: Several equivalent exits dilute the peak.

invariants.rule: Cross once into an obstacle-free large environment and let the camera widen or slow.
invariants.ablation_failure: Continuing dense hazards after the exit cancels the release.

instantiations.concept: An original amber survey submersible races through a flooded coral maintenance trench. Rock ribs, hanging kelp and rotating valve hoops progressively reduce clearance; one final intake tube is the narrowest point, then the craft exits into a vast bioluminescent basin and slows above open water.

Shuttles close from the sides, threads drop overhead and stitched arches narrow the lane; it crosses one final bobbin eye and enters a broad blank cutting table where the camera settles.
